journeys.topology: one external producer submits 16384 short request tiles to four pinned scheduler workers; every callback polls one shared cancellation source, computes a 64-element deterministic tile and publishes one result through a bounded channel
journeys.ownership: the caller owns immutable input, callback records, cancellation root and result drain; the scheduler owns only admitted callback execution; the channel owns exactly one result per admitted callback
charged_phases: external scheduler admission and worker dispatch
bounded channel publication and caller collection
journeys.reason: This is the ordinary short-work route exposed by the installed sched journey; nonzero tile work prevents a zero-callback benchmark from defining product shape.

journeys.topology: one admitted root fiber runs 16 batches that each fan out 128 typed tasks over four workers; each task computes a 1024-element tile, and the root waits for the whole dynamic span and consumes every typed result
journeys.ownership: the caller owns immutable input and the root-lifetime acknowledgement; the root fiber owns dynamic JoinHandles/results; each scheduler task owns its coroutine frame and recycled guarded fiber stack until completion
charged_phases: dynamic when_all and typed result join
journeys.downstream_status: Graph remains QUEUED; this file is provenance for the sched API shape only and grants no Graph verdict.
journeys.reason: The current Graph consumer already runs spawn_task and fan-out completion from a scheduler fiber and floors automatic grains at 1024 elements. The replay retains that structure while keeping graph algorithms outside sched.

journeys.consumer: IO, timer or GPU completion source
journeys.topology: one external completion role drives 4096 episodes; each episode wakes one persistent suspended fiber on each of four pinned workers, blocks for all four acknowledgements without burning a fifth execution role, and then advances
journeys.ownership: each fiber owns and republishes one fresh HYLE Waker per episode; the external source borrows it only through wake(); pinned worker ownership survives suspension and reinjection
journeys.downstream_status: IO is not closed by this evidence; Compute remains QUEUED. These sources prove only the common sched completion contract.
journeys.reason: IO and GPU polling already converge on Waker::wake(); a persistent multi-episode replay measures the normal completion spine instead of fiber construction.

peer_contract.cancellation_submechanism: C++23 std::stop_token from the same MSVC toolchain
peer_contract.equivalence: Candidate and peer use separate processes, the same four physical cores, identical input/tile/count/accounting, persistent scheduler lifetimes and setup exclusions. Marl owns peer scheduling, fiber wait/wake, WaitGroup and channel lock/notification composition; std::stop_token supplies the standard O(1) cancellation poll Marl does not define.

negative_space.zero_work: Historical zero/noop task results remain diagnostic API-cost facts and do not gate the normal nonzero consumer replays.
negative_space.specialized_spmd: ggml-style caller-participating graph execution, pause/resume and chunk policy belong to Graph/Compute or a future inference runtime.
negative_space.downstream_closure: Building IO, Compute or Graph against sched proves compatibility only; it does not validate their functionality or performance.
